subject: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Horizon Health POC sizing
messages:
From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@horizonhealth.com>

Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Horizon Health POC sizing

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the streaming demo helpful. A few clarifications from our side to make sure the POC sizing is realistic: 

- Baseline traffic: about 7k active users weekday peak, roughly 1.8k concurrent prompt requests at peak.
- Request characteristics: average input ~180 tokens, average output ~220 tokens (we'll attach a sample CSV).
- SLA target: p95 end-to-end user-perceived latency <= 250ms for streaming (we accept slightly higher cold-starts).
- Concurrency: we want headroom for 2x burst above peak for seasonal events (so design for ~3.6k concurrent requests).
- Model: planning to use an open LLM (approx 20B footprint); streaming is required for UX.
- Acceptable fallback: brief partial responses followed by non-blocking completion is ok, but we need predictable latency during steady-state.

I'll send the traffic sample and a top-level product requirements doc. Can you confirm whether Redwood will size for tokens/sec or QPS for the POC, and what metrics you need from us to produce a recommended capacity profile?

Thanks,
Sam

Hi Sam — really helpful notes, thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the CSV.  

High level response / next steps from our side: 

1) What we size for: we produce a recommended capacity profile in two complementary ways — tokens/sec throughput (sustained and peak) and QPS/concurrency targets. For streaming-heavy UX we prioritize sustained tokens/sec per-GPU and per-pod concurrency, plus a burst headroom policy.

2) Immediate asks from you (small checklist so we can size quickly):
   - Confirm 95th-percentile output tokens you care about (you gave avg 220; do you expect 95th > 400?).
   - Indicate maximum tolerated cold-start latency for first token (you said slightly higher; please quantify if possible).
   - Any request size variance (e.g., 10% heavy long-form that goes to 2k tokens).

3) What we'll deliver in the POC sizing doc (by EOD Thu):
   - Recommended config: GPU type(s) and number, per-pod concurrency, batch windows, expected tokens/sec per-GPU, estimated steady-state QPS, and peak capacity with 2x buffer.
   - Cost estimate (monthly) for Dedicated pool for the POC timeframe.
   - Suggested caching and KV strategies to reduce per-token compute for repeat prefixes.

Ben and Neha are looping in to run a quick capacity calc — Ben will run an initial tokens/sec projection against a 20B-like model profile; Neha will draft a POC runbook and metrics to capture during testing.  

If you can confirm the 95th percentile output token assumption and the cold-start tolerance by EOD Wednesday, we'll lock the sizing and get a proposal out by Thursday.

Camila

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput & SLO follow-up: Horizon Health POC sizing

Camila / Sam — quick technical note from my end after loading the CSV sample: 

- Observed median input+output token per request ~390 tokens; p95 in sample ~680 tokens (so please confirm if sample is representative).
- For a 20B open model on A100/RTX8000-class hardware, conservative sustained token throughput per GPU is ~1200-1400 tokens/sec when using 8-way batching and quantized runtime.
- That maps to roughly 1 GPU per ~3-4 steady concurrent streaming sessions (depends on how much overlap the streaming windows have).
- To meet p95 <= 250ms perceived latency we recommend the following for POC:
   • Dedicated pool of 8 GPUs (quantized), configured with 256ms batch window max, and KV cache enabled for repeat prefixes.
   • Autoscale policy to add 4 GPUs when CPU queue length exceeds threshold (this gets you ~2x burst headroom).

Action items I'm taking: run a quick simulation (tokens/sec * concurrency distribution across the day) and post an estimated QPS/steady-state number back here by 11:00 PST.  

-Ben

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks Ben — and Camila, yes to the p95 clarification: in our user tests the 95th output token was ~600 tokens (we had a subset of long-form flows). Cold-start tolerance: up to 600ms first token but we need p95 perceived <= 250ms once streaming begins (so first token can be a bit slower).

Confirmed on attachments and the CSV sample being representative of peak weekdays.  The team is comfortable with the proposed Dedicated pool approach for the POC — please send the formal proposal and cost estimate and we'll route for internal approvals.

I'll also share a short list of 3 test user journeys we'll expect to run during the POC.

Sam
